DR . JUSTICE CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA  ORAL JUDGMENT Heard Sri. K.V. Naik, learned counsel for the appellant as well as Sri. Shankara Reddy C., learned counsel who represents respondent No.1-insurance company.
2. The claimant is before this Court seeking enhancement of compensation challenging the order that is rendered by the Motor Accidents Claims Tribunal, Bengaluru, in MVC No.4832/2020 dated 4.11.2022.
The Tribunal through the impugned order awarded a sum of Rs.8,06,531/- as compensation under the following heads.

sentences.text: Future medical expenses 15,000-00  Total 8,06,531-00 3.
Sri . K.V.Naik.,
learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant sustained grievous injury due to the accident and became permanently disabled.
Learned counsel contends that the appellant as a teacher was earning Rs.10,000/- per month by the date of accident.
But due to the injury sustained she became permanently disabled.

Learned counsel also states that without considering the evidence of PW2, the Tribunal awarded a meager sum under the head loss of future earnings due to disability and also loss of income during laid up period which is highly unjustifiable.
Learned counsel thereby seeks for enhancement of compensation.
4. On the other hand, Sri.Shankar Reddy C., learned counsel for respondent No.1 contends that the Tribunal awarded exorbitant sum as compensation.
Learned counsel states that the appellant sustained only one grievous injury, but NC: 2024:KHC:32278 the Tribunal granted a sum of Rs.80,000/- under the head pain and sufferings which is excessive.
Learned counsel also states that under all heads sufficient and substantive sum is awarded as compensation and therefore, the claimant cannot seek more.
5. As per the material available on record, the appellant sustained fracture of left proximal tibia.
PW3 deposed that the disability in respect of whole body is 13%.
However, considering the totality of evidence, the Tribunal took permanent functional disability as 10% in respect of the whole body.
The said finding is sound and convincing.
The appellant did not produce any proof with regard to her actual occupation, income by the date of accident.
The Tribunal took the notional income of the appellant as Rs.14,500/- per month.
The said sum is reasonable.
Also taking into consideration the fact that the appellant took treatment as inpatient for two weeks, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.29,000/- towards loss of income during laid up period.

Also apart from awarding a sum of Rs.80,000/- under the head pain and sufferings, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.20,000/-
towards conveyance charges, Rs.50,000/- towards food, nourishment, attendant charges and loss of amenities and Rs.15,000/- towards future medical NC: 2024:KHC:32278 expenses.
Assessing the permanent functional disability as 10%, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.3,13,200/- towards loss of future income.
Also basing on the medical bills produced, the Tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.2,99,331/- which is the amount that was spent by the appellant for her treatment.

Thus,
reasonable amount was awarded as compensation under all heads.
Therefore, this Court is of the view that there are no grounds to interfere with.
Resultantly, the appeal stands dismissed without costs.

Sd/- 
(DR.CHILLAKUR SUMALATHA) JUDGE AP
